quote.translation: The determination of "identity", and with it of "the necessary", is found in three places, in conceptuality, in groundedness and in wholeness.

quote.translation: This is to say that it is grasped in (1) the relation between a concept and its marks, (2) the relation between ground and consequent, and (3) the relation between whole and part.

regions.text: 「普遍約判断（二二貫参照を造つて頬概念甲の中にそれ自身既に思催されてゐるやうなこを求める。さうすればこの乙は必然に甲の各々の種に鯖屬する。二假説約判断を造つて、おといふ條件が甲に加はることによつてこの修件なしには存在しないであらうところの乙がその甲に生ずることを示す。さうすれば同様の條件が同機の仕方で作用を及ぼすところの各々の甲に開してこの乙は必然前に妥営する。

quote.translation: Lotze identifies three forms that lead to necessary knowledge of the relation between two terms, A and B. In the first, we form a generic judgement (see p. 22) and seek a B that is already thought within the generic concept A, so that B necessarily belongs to every species of A. In the second, we form a hypothetical judgement and show that when a condition x is added to A, a B arises in that A which would not otherwise exist, so that B holds necessarily of every A on which the same condition acts in the same way.

regions.text: 自離接約判斷を造つ、て、或る間題を嚴密な「一か他か」へ還元するならば、それと同時に事態を確實に握るやうになる。さうすればもはや一つの経驗を要するだけで、各々の個々の場合に於て乙か丙か二つの逃語のうちのいつれが甲に開して必然性を有つて措定されるかを決定することが出来る。

quote.translation: In the third, we form a disjunctive judgement, reducing a problem to a strict "either the one or the other", and so gain a firm hold on the state of affairs, since a single experience then suffices to decide, in each case, which of the two predicates, B or C, is posited of A with necessity.
For Lotze the ways of arriving at necessary knowledge are limited to these three, and there is no other (Lotze, Logik, hrsg. v. Misch, Leipzig, 1912, S. 65).
